skill.name: build-design
skill.description: Builds UI from a Figma file or a design image so it matches the design, using the project's existing tokens and components.
skill.summary: Implement Figma frames or reference images with existing project components, then report visual differences and missing connections.
skill.author: jakubkrehel

security_audit.summary: All nine static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, Figma tool discovery, image estimation, or local visual comparison. One semantic finding identifies possible loss of existing user changes through unqualified instructions to revert unrelated files. No evidence found of credential theft, screenshot uploads, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The instruction to revert files outside the design scope does not distinguish agent edits from existing user changes.
remediation.suggestion: Record existing changes before implementation. Undo only edits made during this task, preserve user changes, and request approval when ownership is uncertain.

content.user_title: Build Interfaces from Figma and Design Images
content.value_statement: Implementing a design can introduce inconsistent spacing, components, and unsupported visual choices. This skill maps reference designs to existing project tokens and compares the implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guide Figma tool discovery and retrieve frame context, screenshots, variables, and component mappings.
Estimate dimensions from reference images while declaring the assumed scale.
Map design values and component instances to existing project tokens and components.
Implement scoped frames, specified breakpoints, and states shown in the design.
Compare rendered interfaces against reference frames at their intended widths.
Report rounded values, deviations, unwired data, missing states, and domain conflicts.
limitations: Figma workflows require an available, authenticated MCP integration.
Image-only references provide estimated measurements rather than exact design values.
Visual comparison remains unverified without browser access or rendered screenshots.
Missing backend integrations remain props-based, and unspecified states use existing component defaults.

use_cases.title: Implement Product Frames
use_cases.description: Build selected Figma frames with established components and document any token rounding.

use_cases.title: Compare Design Handoffs
use_cases.description: Check implemented screens against reference widths and receive a property-based difference report.

use_cases.title: Prototype from Reference Images
use_cases.description: Turn supplied images into scoped interface work with explicit measurement assumptions and backend gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Build One Reference Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the screen in [image] using this project's existing tokens and components. State measurement assumptions and preserve existing user changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: implement a single image reference.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Selected Figma Frames
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [frame links] from [Figma URL]. Read design values through Figma tools, reuse existing components, and report rounding or missing equivalents.

prompt_templates.title: Build Responsive States
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [desktop and mobile frames] with their specified states. Compare each frame width and list unwired data, missing states, and unresolved domain conflicts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: coordinate breakpoints and component states.

prompt_templates.title: Implement and Verify a Scoped Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [frames] in [project area] and compare rendered screenshots at every supplied width. Preserve pre-existing changes and request approval before any unrelated revert.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: deliver a verified change in an active workspace.

output_examples.input: Implement a card with 20-pixel padding and a 15-pixel title using existing tokens.
output: Card padding: design 20 pixels; implementation 20 pixels through the existing spacing token; matches.
Title size: design 15 pixels; implementation 14 pixels through the existing text token; rounded.
Badge: no matching component exists; deviation reported for approval.

output_examples.input: Build the supplied mobile and desktop frames when browser access and the backend are unavailable.
output: Both supplied frame widths implemented using existing components.
Unwired: account details render from props until the backend is available.
Missing states: loading and error are absent from the supplied design.
Visual comparison: unverified because browser rendering was unavailable.

best_practices: Provide exact frame links and intended viewport widths before implementation.
Identify project tokens and components, and resolve accessibility conflicts before accepting design fidelity.
Record existing workspace changes and approve only task-owned reversions.
anti_patterns: Claiming exact design measurements from screenshots without declaring estimation assumptions.
Adding new tokens, component variants, or arbitrary values without approval.
Reverting unrelated files without checking whether their changes belong to the user.

faq.question: Which design inputs are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow accepts Figma links, screenshots, and exported design images. Figma provides exact values; image measurements are estimates.

faq.question: Does it require a Figma integration?
faq.answer: Figma links require an available, authenticated MCP integration. Image-based work does not require Figma access.

faq.question: Will it create a new design system?
faq.answer: No. It reuses project tokens and components, reports missing equivalents, and asks before visibly significant rounding.

faq.question: Does it implement missing backend services?
faq.answer: No. It renders affected UI from props and lists those areas as unwired.

faq.question: Can it verify a visual match without a browser?
faq.answer: No. It should provide the local URL and widths to check, then clearly state that visual comparison remains unverified.

faq.question: What safety precaution matters in an active workspace?
faq.answer: Preserve existing user changes. The skill contains an unqualified revert instruction, so limit any reversal to verified task-owned edits.
